rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In فَلَا أُقْسِمُ, the لا is an emphatic extra particle, so the phrase means ‘I swear,’ like the usage in 57:29.
rows.anchor: معناه فأقسم . ولا مزيدة مؤكدة مثلها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads فلأقسم, understood as ‘I indeed swear’: an initial lām governs an underlying أنا أقسم clause whose subject is omitted.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : ( فلأقسم ) . ومعناه : فلأنا أقسم : اللام لام الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām is not an oath particle: it lacks the normally required emphatic nūn, and an oath's response is future while the oath itself is present.
rows.anchor: ولا يصح أن نكون اللام لام القسم لأمرين ، أحدهما : أن حقها أن يقرن بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stars' settings may be a moment of special divine acts, angelic worship, night prayer, and descending mercy, explaining the oath's declared greatness.
rows.anchor: بمساقطها ومغاربها ، لعل لله تعالى في آخر الليل إذا انحطت النجوم إلى المغرب أفعالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the stars' stations and courses display a measure of divine power and wisdom beyond description.
rows.anchor: أو أراد بمواقعها : منازلها ومسايرها ، وله تعالى في ذلك من الدليل على عظيم القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that this is a tremendous oath interrupts between oath and its answer; لو تعلمون further interrupts between the described noun and adjective.
rows.anchor: اعتراض في اعتراض ؛ لأنه اعترض به بين المقسم والمقسم عليه ، وهو قوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the stars' positions as the times when Qur'anic passages descended in installments.
rows.anchor: وقيل : مواقع النجوم : أوقات وقوع نجوم القرآن ، أي : أوقات نزولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is noble—excellent in its kind, beneficial, or honored by God—and the protected book is inaccessible to all but purified angels if it means the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: كريم حسن مرضي في جنسه من الكتب . أو نفاع جم المنافع . أو كريم على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the protected book describes the Qur'an, only a person ritually pure should touch its written copy; some extend this to recitation.
rows.anchor: وإن جعلتها صفة للقرآن ؛ فالمعنى لا ينبغي أن يمسه إلا من هو على الطهارة من الناس

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar preferred that a person recite only while ritually pure.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عمر أحب إلي أن لا يقرأ إلا وهو طاهر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In one transmission, Ibn Abbas permitted a person in major ritual impurity to recite.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس في رواية أنه كان يبيح القراءة للجنب

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet's saying that a Muslim is his fellow Muslim's brother illustrates the preceding wording about what one ought not do.
rows.anchor: ( المسلم أخو المسلم لا يظلمه ولا يسلمه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings المتطهرون and المطهرون use assimilation; المطهرون can also derive from form IV, while المطهرون may mean those who purify themselves or angels purifying others through prayer and revelation.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( المتطهرون ) والمطهرون بالإدغام . والمطهرون ، من أطهره بمعنى طهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تنزيل is a fourth adjective for the Qur'an, meaning sent down from the Lord of the worlds; alternatively it is a verbal noun because the Qur'an descended in installments.
rows.anchor: { تنزيل } صفة رابعة للقرآن ، أي : منزل من رب العالمين . أو وصف بالمصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a verbal noun, تنزيل became nearly a name for the Qur'an, as in saying that something occurs ‘in the Tanzīl.’
rows.anchor: فكأنه في نفسه تنزيل ؛ ولذلك جرى مجرى بعض أسمائه ، فقيل : جاء في التنزيل كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may instead use تنزيل as a predicate after a fronted nominal subject; another reading has the accusative تنزيلا as a cognate accusative.
rows.anchor: أو هو تنزيل على حرف المبتدأ . وقرىء : ( تنزيلا ) على : نزل تنزيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth distracts through its management, pursuit of growth and profit, trade, and enjoyment; children distract through affection, care, and providing for their needs during life and after one's death.
rows.anchor: لا تشغلكم { أموالكم } والتصرف فيها : والسعي في تدبير أمرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers already know that wealth and children are slight beside what God has, so remembrance of God must take precedence over them.
rows.anchor: وقد عرفتم قدر منفعة الأموال والأولاد ، وأنه أهون شيء وأدونه في جنب ما عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being occupied with worldly life at the expense of religion makes people lose their trade by exchanging the lasting good for a paltry, passing thing.
rows.anchor: يريد الشغل بالدنيا عن الدين { فأولئك هم الخاسرون } في تجارتهم حيث باعوا العظيم الباقي بالحقير الفاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation identifies remembrance of God with the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ذكر الله الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets remembrance as all religious duties, effectively obedience to God.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : جميع الفرائض ، كأنه قال : عن طاعة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation identifies remembrance with the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وقيل : القرآن . وعن الكلبي : الجهاد

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets remembrance as fighting alongside the Messenger of God.
rows.anchor: وعن الكلبي : الجهاد مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The مِن in مما رزقناكم is partitive; the required spending is intended.
rows.anchor: {من} في { ما رزقناكم } للتبعيض ، والمراد : الإنفاق الواجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning applies before death's signs become unmistakable, when one can no longer hope for respite, give acceptably, or avoid regret over withheld charity.
rows.anchor: { من قبل أن يأتى أحدكم الموت } من قبل أن يرى دلائل الموت ، ويعاين ما ييأس معه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas urges charity before death's authority arrives, when a capable person will not be accepted.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : تصدقوا قبل أن ينزل عليكم سلطان الموت ، فلا تقبل توبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas urges anyone with wealth to pay zakah and anyone able to perform pilgrimage to do so before death; a request to return will then be refused.
rows.anchor: وعنه : ما يمنع أحدكم إذا كان له مال أن يزكي ، وإذا أطاق الحج أن يحج

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the passage concerns those withholding zakah; he argues that a person who had seen good would not seek to return, and identifies believers as its addressees.
rows.anchor: وعنه : أنها نزلت في ما نعى الزكاة ، ووالله لو رأى خيرا لما سأل الرجعة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan likewise says anyone who failed to give zakah, fast, or perform pilgrimage will ask to return at death.
rows.anchor: وكذا عن الحسن : ما من أحد لم يزك ولم يصم ولم يحج إلا سأل الرجعة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the verse was revealed concerning the people of the qibla.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة أنها نزلت في أهل القبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The variant أخرتن means ‘Why did You not delay my death?’; a nearby term means a short period.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( أخرتن ) ، يريد : هلا أخرت موتى

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy reads فأتصدق, preserving the fuller form of the verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي فأتصدق على الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading وأكن joins the jussive to the grammatical position of فأصدق, meaning ‘if delayed, I would give and become’; وأكون instead follows the overt form.
rows.anchor: على محل { فأصدق } كأنه قيل : إن أخرتني أصدق وأكن

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr reads وأكون as if the speaker promises, ‘and I shall be’ righteous.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبيد بن عمير : ( وأكون ) ، على ( وأنا أكون ) عدة منه بالصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic denial that God delays a soul means such delay would conflict with wisdom; knowing death is unavoidable and deeds judged requires prompt fulfillment of duties and readiness to meet God.
rows.anchor: نفي للتأخير على وجه التأكيد الذي معناه منافاة المنفي الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing verb is also read with either second-person plural or third-person plural inflection.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( تعملون ) ؛ بالتاء والياء

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises freedom from hypocrisy for whoever recites Surat al-Munafiqun.
rows.anchor: ( 1187 ) ( من قرأ سورة المنافقين بريء من النفاق )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People asked what waiting period applies to women who do not menstruate; the passage was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: روي أن ناسا قالوا : قد عرفنا عدة ذوات الأقراء ، فما عدة اللائي لا يحضن ؛ فنزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن ارتبتم means either uncertainty about the ruling, or uncertainty whether bleeding in women thought to have reached menopause (estimated at sixty or fifty-five) is menstruation or irregular bleeding; their term is three months, and women without doubt follow a fortiori.
rows.anchor: فمعنى { إن ارتبتم } : إن أشكل عليكم حكمهن وجهلتم كيف يعتددن فهذا حكمهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who have not menstruated are young girls; the clause ‘their waiting period is three months’ is omitted because the preceding wording supplies it.
rows.anchor: هن الصغائر . والمعنى : فعدتهن ثلاثة أشهر ، فحذف لدلالة المذكور عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unqualified wording for pregnant women includes both divorced women and widows.
rows.anchor: اللفظ مطلق في أولات الأحمال ، فاشتمل على المطلقات والمتوفى عنهن

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud, Ubayy, Abu Hurayra, and others did not distinguish a pregnant widow's waiting period from that of other pregnant women.
rows.anchor: وكان ابن مسعود وأبي وأبو هريرة وغيرهم لا يفرقون

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali and Ibn Abbas hold that a pregnant widow waits for the later of the two terms.
rows.anchor: وعن علي وابن عباس : عدة الحامل المتوفى عنها أبعد الأجلين

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah offers to swear that the shorter Surat al-Nisa was revealed after the one in al-Baqara, supporting the unqualified rule for pregnant women.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الله : من شاء لاعنته أن سورة النساء القصرى نزلت بعد التي في البقرة

rows.speaker: أم سلمة
rows.claim: Umm Salama reports that Subay'a al-Aslamiyya gave birth a few nights after her husband's death; the Prophet told her that she was free to marry.
rows.anchor: وروت أم سلمة : ( 1203 ) أن سبيعة الأسلمية ولدت بعد وفاة زوجها بليال ، فذكرت ذلك لرسول الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told Subay'a, after her delivery, ‘You are free’; the report establishes her waiting period had ended.
rows.anchor: فقال لها : قد حللت فأنكحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes the affairs and knots of a person who acts by these rulings in piety easier; observing the specified housing, non-harm, support, and nursing-wage duties earns forgiveness and great reward.
rows.anchor: ومن يتق الله في العمل بما أنزل الله من هذه الأحكام وحافظ على الحقوق الواجبة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mecca's people were tested with famine through the Prophet's supplication against them; the garden owners were pious worshippers near San'a.
rows.anchor: إنا بلونا أهل مكة بالقحط والجوع بدعوة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their father kept a year's food and gave the surplus to the poor, including missed grain, grapes, and dates; his sons feared hardship for their dependents and secretly swore to harvest early without leaving any share.
rows.anchor: فكان يأخذ منها قوت سنته ويتصدق بالباقي ، وكان يترك للمساكين ما أخطأه المنجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sons did not make an exception in their oath, and God burned their garden; another report identifies them as Israelites.
rows.anchor: فحلفوا ليصرمنها مصبحين في السدف خفية عن المساكين ، ولم يستثنوا في يمينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They planned to harvest early in the dark before dawn; not making an exception means not saying ‘if God wills.’ Though a condition, it functions as an exception because the meanings coincide.
rows.anchor: { مصبحين } داخلين في الصبح مبكرين { ولا يستثنون } ولا يقولون إن شاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The calamity that swept the garden was a trial or destruction; the reading طيف varies from طائف.
rows.anchor: { فطاف عليها } بلاء أو هلاك { طئف } كقوله تعالى : { وأحيط بثمره }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الصريم may mean a garden cut down, a night-blackened garden, dried daytime vegetation, an empty garden, or sandy ground; صارمين means harvesters.
rows.anchor: { فأصبحت كالصريم } كالمصرومة لهلاك ثمرها . وقيل : الصريم الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase غدوا على حرثكم uses على because they went to cut and harvest it; alternatively غدا is understood as ‘turned toward,’ as in the expression ‘the enemy went against them.’
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يضمن الغدو معنى الإقبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يتخافتون means whispering; خفي, خفت, and خفد all denote concealment, and الخفدود is a bat.
rows.anchor: { يتخافتون } يتسارون فيما بينهم . وخفى ، وخفت ، وخفد : ثلاثتها في معنى الكتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase أن لا يدخلنها is explanatory; Ibn Masud reads without أن, supplying ‘they say.’ The ban on a poor person entering means not allowing him in.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود بطرحها بإضمار القول ، أي تخافتون يقولون لا يدخلنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حرد can mean a year withholding its good, camels withholding milk, or resolve and speed; the sons went out aiming to deprive the poor but found only deprivation themselves.
rows.anchor: الحرد : من حردت السنة إذا منعت خيرها ؛ وحاردت الإبل إذا منعت درها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading على حرد means they could manage only anger at one another, as in the next phrase ‘blaming one another.’
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( على حرد ) ، أي لم يقدروا إلا على حنق وغضب بعضهم على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line uses حرد for setting out quickly; birds called حراد are swift, so the sons thought they could promptly harvest and deny the poor their share.
rows.anchor: أقبل سيل جاء من أمر الله … يحرد حرد الجنة المغلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حرد may instead be the proper name of the garden, or mean that they assumed their planned harvest and deprivation would succeed.
rows.anchor: وقيل : { حرد } علم للجنة ، أي غدوا على تلك الجنة قادرين على صرامها عند أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They first thought they had lost their way because the ruined garden looked unlike theirs; after recognizing it, they admitted they had been deprived through their own wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: { إنا لضالون } أي ضللنا جنتنا ، وما هي بها لما رأوا من هلاكها ؛ فلما تأملوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أوسطهم means their most just and best member, from language for someone in the middle of their people; compare the description of the community as a middle community.
rows.anchor: { أوسطهم } أعدلهم وخيرهم ، من قولهم : هو من سطة قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لولا تسبحون most likely means remember God and repent of the corrupt plan; the speaker had urged them to repent before punishment, but they obeyed too late.
rows.anchor: لولا تذكرون الله وتتوبون إليه من خبث نيتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes ‘glorify’ to mean making the exception ‘if God wills,’ since both entrusting matters to God and declaring His transcendence magnify Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالتسبيح . الاستثناء لالتقائهما في معنى التعظيم لله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says it means prayer; their neglect of prayer would explain why it did not restrain wrongdoing and prompt an exception.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : هو الصلاة ، كأنهم كانوا يتوانون في الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By saying ‘Glory be to our Lord,’ they deny that God is unjust and confess their own wrongdoing in withholding charity and failing to make an exception.
rows.anchor: { سبحان ربنا } سبحوا الله ونزهوه عن الظلم وعن كل قبيح ، ثم اعترفوا بظلمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They blamed one another because some proposed the plan, some accepted it, some opposed it, and others remained silent in approval.
rows.anchor: { يتلاومون } يلوم بعضهم بعضا ؛ لأن منهم من زين ، ومنهم من قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb يبدلنا has readings with and without doubling; راغبون إلى ربنا means seeking good from Him and hoping for His pardon.
rows.anchor: { أن يبدلنا } قرىء بالتشديد والتخفيف { إلى ربنا راغبون } طالبون منه الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment resembles that of Mecca's people and the garden owners, but the punishment of the afterlife is greater.
rows.anchor: { كذلك العذاب } مثل ذلك العذاب الذي بلونا به أهل مكة وأصحاب الجنة عذاب الدنيا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: When asked whether the garden owners belong to Paradise or Hell, Qatada replied that the question had burdened him.
rows.anchor: وسئل قتادة عن أصحاب الجنة : أهم من أهل الجنة أم من أهل النار ؟ فقال : لقد كلفتني تعبا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the owners repented and were given a better garden.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد : تابوا فأبدلوا خيرا منها

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that they became sincere and God replaced the garden with one called al-Hayawan, whose grape clusters required a donkey to carry.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه : بلغني أنهم أخلصوا وعرف الله منهم الصدق فأبدلهم بها جنة يقال لها الحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here الإنسان means people generally, which is why worshippers are excepted from the description of being halūʿ.
rows.anchor: أريد بالإنسان الناس ؛ فلذلك استثنى منه إلا المصلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Halūʿ describes quick despair when harmed and quick withholding when good arrives; its root suggests a fast-moving she-camel.
rows.anchor: والهلع : سرعة الجزع عند مس المكروه وسرعة المنع عند مس الخير

rows.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
rows.claim: Asked by Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Tahir what halūʿ means, Ahmad ibn Yahya answered that God's own explanation is the clearest: despair in hardship and withholding in prosperity.
rows.anchor: وعن أحمد بن يحيى ، قال لي محمد بن عبد الله بن طاهر : ما الهلع ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good and evil may mean wealth and poverty, or health and sickness: a healthy rich person withholds charity, while illness makes him complain and give instructions.
rows.anchor: والخير : المال والغنى ؛ والشر : الفقر . أو الصحة والمرض : إذا صح الغني منع المعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are so habituated to despair and withholding that these seem innate, as in ‘the human was created hasty’; yet the description is learned, since infants lack it and believers discipline themselves against it.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { خلق الإنسان من عجل } ( الأنبياء : 37 )

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet calls a miserly, despairing disposition and a fear that strips one of courage among the worst gifts given to Adam's son.
rows.anchor: شر ما أعطى ابن آدم شح هالع وجبن خالع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being constant in prayer means performing it regularly without neglect or distraction; guarding prayer means perfecting ablution, timing, pillars, sunnah, manners, and protection from sins that void it.
rows.anchor: معنى دوامهم عليها أن يواظبوا على أدائها لا يخلون بها ولا يشتغلون عنها بشيء من الشواغل

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says the best work is that done most consistently, even when little.
rows.anchor: أفضل العمل أدومه وإن قل

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says the Prophet's practice was continuous and regular.
rows.anchor: وقول عائشة : ( 1228 ) كان عمله ديمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘known due’ means zakah, or a person may assign himself charity and pay it at known times; the petitioner asks, while the deprived is too self-restrained to ask and is mistaken for rich.
rows.anchor: { حق معلوم } هو الزكاة ، لأنها مقدرة معلومة ؛ أو صدقة يوظفها الرجل على نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They affirm the Judgment Day by their conduct and preparation and fear their Lord's punishment; no one should feel entirely safe, but should balance fear with hope.
rows.anchor: تصديقا بأعمالهم واستعدادهم له ، ويشفقون من عذاب ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading is either singular شهادة or plural شهادات; testimony is singled out among trusts because keeping it alive validates rights, while distorting it destroys them.
rows.anchor: والشهادة من جملة الأمانات . وخصها من بينها إبانة لفضلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عبد الله means the Prophet. The wording reflects the Prophet speaking of himself with humility, or stresses that God's servant worshipping Him is rational and unsurprising.
rows.anchor: { عبد الله } النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم . فإن قلت : هلا قيل : رسول الله أو النبي ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قام يدعوه means he rose to worship, specifically for dawn prayer at Nakhlah when jinn came and listened to his recitation.
rows.anchor: ( قام يدعوه ) قام يعبده ، يريد : قيامه لصلاة الفجر بنخلة حين أتاه الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says the jinn crowded around Muhammad in wonder at his worship, the companions' example, and the extraordinary Qur'an they heard.
rows.anchor: { كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا } أي يزدحمون عليه متراكمين تعجبا مما رأوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the polytheists nearly swarmed against him in united opposition when he preached worship of God alone.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه : لما قام رسولا يعبد الله وحده مخالفا للمشركين في عبادتهم الآلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لبدا is a heap, with readings لبدا, لبدا, and لبدا representing the collective pile or plural forms like ساجد/سجد and صبور/صبر.
rows.anchor: { لبدا } جمع لبدة وهو ما تلبد بعضه على بعض ، ومنها ( لبدة الأسد )

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says humans and jinn gathered against the Prophet to extinguish his mission, but God chose to support and make him prevail.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة : تلبدت الإنس والجن على هذا الأمر ليطفئوه فأبى الله إلا أن ينصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra on وإنه, the words become the jinn's report to their people about what they saw of the Prophet's prayer and his companions crowding to follow him.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ ( وإنه ) بالكسر : جعله من كلام الجن : قالوه لقومهم حين رجعوا إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: برق البصر means the eye is stunned in terror, from looking at lightning and being dazzled; another reading from ‘shine’ means its fixed gaze gleams, while Abu al-Sammal reads بلق, ‘opened.’
rows.anchor: { برق البصر } تحير فزعا ؛ وأصله من برق الرجل إذا نظر إلى البرق فدهش بصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon's light may disappear, or the moon itself may disappear; another reading uses the passive voice.
rows.anchor: { وخسف القمر } وذهب ضوؤه ، أو ذهب بنفسه . وقرىء : ( وخسف ) على البناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon may be gathered as they rise in the west, gathered in losing their light, turned black like two slaughtered oxen in the Fire, or thrown together into the sea as the great Fire.
rows.anchor: { وجمع الشمس والقمر } حيث يطلعهما الله من المغرب . وقيل : وجمعا في ذهاب الضوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المفر with fatḥa is the act of escape, while with kasra it is a place of escape, though the latter can also be a verbal noun; both are read, and كلا rebuffs any search for escape.
rows.anchor: { المفر } بالفتح المصدر ؛ وبالكسر : المكان . ويجوز أن يكون مصدرا كالمرجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no refuge: every mountain or other place one might flee to is called a وزر.
rows.anchor: { كلا } ردع عن طلب المفر { لا } لا ملجأ ، وكل ما التجأت إليه من جبل أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servants' fixed place may be their settlement before God, their return to His judgment alone, or their final place in Paradise or Hell, which He assigns by His will.
rows.anchor: { إلى ربك } خاصة { يومئذ } مستقر العباد ، أي استقرارهم . يعني : أنهم لا يقدرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person is told of deeds done and left undone, wealth given away or left as an inheritance, good and evil acts, and good or bad practices continued by others; Mujahid says it means one's first and last deeds.
rows.anchor: { بما قدم } من عمل عمله { * و } بما { إلاها ءاخر } منه لم يعمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person's own actions are بصيرة, a clear proof or an actual seeing witness; even without being told, the person knows because the limbs testify.
rows.anchor: { بصيرة } حجة بينة وصفت بالبصارة على المجاز ، كما وصفت الآيات بالإبصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولو ألقى معاذيره means however many excuses someone offers; al-Dahhak says it can mean ‘even if he lets down his curtains,’ if that report is sound, since excuses conceal blame as curtains conceal a person.
rows.anchor: ولو جاء بكل معذرة يعتذر بها عن نفسه ويجادل عنها

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets المعاذير as curtains and says the phrase can mean even if the person lets down his curtains.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك : ولو أرخى ستوره ، وقال : المعاذير الستور ، واحدها معذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: معاذير is not the plural of معذرة but a collective noun, like مناكير for منكر.
rows.anchor: المعاذير ليس بجمع معذرة ، إنما هو اسم جمع لها ، ونحوه : المناكير في المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلا rebukes those asking mockingly; سيعلمون threatens that they will learn the matter they mock is true and inevitable.
rows.anchor: كلا} ردع للمتسائلين هزؤا . و { سيعلمون } وعيد لهم بأنهم سوف يعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the rebuke and threat intensifies it; ثم signals that the second threat is stronger than the first.
rows.anchor: وتكرير الردع مع الوعيد تشديد في ذلك ومعنى { ثم } الإشعار بأن الوعيد الثاني أبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed time is a boundary fixed in God's decree at which the world ends, or a boundary toward which all creatures are gathered.
rows.anchor: { كان ميقاتا } كان في تقدير الله وحكمه حدا توقت به الدنيا وتنتهي عنده ؛ أو حدا للخلائق ينتهون إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يوم ينفخ is apposition or explanatory apposition to يوم الفصل; people come in groups from their graves to the assembly, each community with its leader, or as different groups.
rows.anchor: { يوم ينفخ } بدل من يوم الفصل ، أو عطف بيان { فتأتون أفواجا } من القبور إلى الموقف

rows.speaker: معاذ
rows.claim: Muadh asked the Prophet about the great matter; a report describes ten classes of the community resurrected in grotesque forms according to their sins.
rows.anchor: وعن معاذ رضي الله عنه أنه سأل عنه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : ( 1262 ) يا معاذ

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The report assigns ape-like forms to talebearers, pig-like forms to illicit gainers, and face-down crawling to usurers.
rows.anchor: فأما الذين على صورة القردة فالتقات من الناس . وأما الذين على صورة الخنازير : فأهل السحت

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the report, the blind are unjust judges and the deaf-mute are self-admiring people; those chewing their tongues are scholars and storytellers whose deeds contradict their words.
rows.anchor: وأما العمى فالذين يجورون في الحكم ، وأما الصم البكم فالمعجبون بأعمالهم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The report says people who harm neighbors have severed limbs, and informers who carry people to rulers are crucified on trunks of fire.
rows.anchor: وأما الذين قطعت أيديهم وأرجلهم فهم الذين يؤذون الجيران ، وأما المصلبون على جذوع من نار

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The report gives a foul odor to those who follow lusts and withhold God's due from their wealth, and tar garments to the arrogant and boastful.
rows.anchor: أشد نتنا من الجيف فالذين يتبعون الشهوات واللذات ومنعوا حق الله في أموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gates of heaven are read with or without doubling; the opened gates may be pictured as innumerable because angels descend through them, like the earth becoming all springs.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( وفتحت ) بالتشديد والتخفيف . والمعنى : كثرة أبوابها المفتحة لنزول الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the gates are paths and passages opened when heaven is folded away.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الأبواب الطرق والمسالك ، أي : تكشط فينفتح مكانها وتصير طرقا يسدها شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains becoming mirage means they turn into something like nothing as their parts disperse, as in the description of scattered dust.
rows.anchor: { فكانت سرابا } ، كقوله : { فكانت هباء منبثا } ( الواقعة : 6 ) . يعني أنها تصير شيئا كلا شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الطامة is a calamity that overtops and overcomes every other calamity, as in the proverb about a river overrunning villages; it is the Resurrection because of its overwhelming force.
rows.anchor: الطآمة } الداهية التي تطم على الدواهي ، أي : تعلو وتغلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternative identifications are the second trumpet blast or the moment the people of Paradise and Hell are driven to their destinations.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي النفخة الثانية . وقيل : الساعة التي تساق فيها أهل الجنة إلى الجنة وأهل النار إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يوم يتذكر is an apposition to إذا جاءت: when people see their recorded deeds, they remember what they had forgotten.
rows.anchor: { يوم يتذكر } بدل من إذا جاءت ، يعني : إذا رأى أعماله مدونة في كتابه تذكرها وكان قد نسيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما in ما سعى may be a relative pronoun or a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: { ما } في { ما سعى } موصولة ، أو مصدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: برزت means ‘made manifest’; Abu Nuhayk has a doubled reading.
rows.anchor: { وبرزت } أظهرت وقرأ أبو نهيك ( وبرزت )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لمن يرى means visible to every observer; Ibn Masud reads لمن رأى, while Ikrima reads لمن ترى, with the pronoun referring to Hell as in 25:12, or addressed to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود ( لمن رأى ) وقرأ عكرمة ( لمن ترى ) والضمير للجحيم ، كقوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response after فإذا is ‘then the matter is as follows’; الجحيم هي المأوى means Hell is his abode, with a known possessor understood rather than expressed, and هي is either a separator or subject.
rows.anchor: أي : فإذا جاءت الطاقة فإن الأمر كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is the self that commands evil; destructive desire means following appetites, which one must restrain and discipline through patience and preference for good.
rows.anchor: { ونهى النفس } الأمارة بالسوء { عن الهوى } المردي وهو اتباع الشهوات وزجرها عنه وضبطها بالصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says these verses were revealed about Abu Aziz ibn Umayr and Mus'ab ibn Umayr: Mus'ab killed his brother at Uhud and defended the Messenger until struck by arrows.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الآيتان نزلتا في أبي عزيز بن عمير ومصعب بن عمير ، وقد قتل مصعب أخاه أبا عزير يوم أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أيان مرساها asks when the Hour will be established and brought into being; alternatively it asks for its end or resting place, like a ship's anchorage.
rows.anchor: متى إرساؤها ، أي إقامتها ، أرادوا : متى يقيمها الله ويثبتها ويكونها ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading asks what place the Prophet occupies in telling them its time; Aisha reports that he kept mentioning and asking about the Hour until this verse descended, expressing wonder at his concern.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها : ( 1266 ) لم يزل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يذكر الساعة يسأل عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the question rebukes their asking: the Prophet's sending as the final messenger is itself a sign of the Hour's nearness and a reason to prepare, so asking its date is pointless.
rows.anchor: وقيل : { فيم } إنكار لسؤالهم ، أي فيم هذا السؤال ، ثم قيل : أنت من ذكراها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge of the Hour ends with God and has not been given to any created being.
rows.anchor: { إلى ربك منتهاها } أي منتهى علمها لم يؤت علمها أحدا من خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was sent to warn those who may be moved to fear by the Hour's terrors, not to teach its date, which would be of no benefit.
rows.anchor: { إنما أنت منذر من يخشاها } أي : لم تبعث لتعلمهم بوقت الساعة الذي لا فائدة لهم في علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: منذر may be read with tanwin; the construct reading is a lighter form. Both can denote present or future, while past meaning requires the construct form.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( منذر ) بالتنوين ، وهو الأصل ؛ والإضافة تخفيف ، وكلاهما يصلح للحال والاستقبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People seem to have lived in the world—or in the graves—only an evening or its morning; adding the morning to evening marks less than a full day, just an hour of it.
rows.anchor: كأنهم لم يلبثوا في الدنيا ، وقيل : في القبور

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises that whoever recites Surat al-Nazi'at will be held in the grave and at the Resurrection only as long as an obligatory prayer, then enter Paradise.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة والنازعات كان ممن حبسه الله في القبر والقيامة حتى يدخل الجنة قدر صلاة المكتوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath is by dawn, as in other dawn descriptions, or by the dawn prayer.
rows.anchor: أقسم بالفجر كما أقسم بالصبح في قوله : { والصبح إذا أسفر } ( المدثر : 34 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten nights are the first ten of Dhu al-Hijja. Their indefiniteness marks them as a specially virtuous subset of nights; definite wording would lose that emphasis and disrupt the matching oath forms.
rows.anchor: أراد بالليالي العشر : عشر ذي الحجة . فإن قلت : فما بالها منكرة من بين ما أقسم به ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The even and odd may mean all even and odd things, or the even and odd among these nights; alternatively, the even is the Day of Sacrifice and the odd is the Day of Arafah.
rows.anchor: وبالشفع والوتر : إما الأشياء كلها شفعها ووترها ، وإما شفع هذه الليالي ووترها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet interpreted the even and odd as the Day of Sacrifice and the Day of Arafah.
rows.anchor: وقد ( 1299 ) روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه فسرهما بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The many further interpretations of even and odd add little and are fit to be left aside rather than pursued to exhaustion.
rows.anchor: وقد أكثروا في الشفع والوتر حتى كادوا يستوعبون أجناس ما يقعان فيه ، وذلك قليل الطائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general night is sworn by when it passes, as in other descriptions of the departing night.
rows.anchor: وبعد ما أقسم بالليالي المخصوصة أقسم بالليل على العموم { إذا يسر } إذا يمضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وَالوتر is also read with a fatḥa on wāw; another reading has fatḥa on wāw and kasra on tāʾ, transmitted by Yunus from Abu Amr.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( والوتر ) بفتح الواو ، وهما لغتان كالحبر والحبر في العدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading joins al-fajr and al-watr with tanwin, which substitutes for a final lengthening letter; Ibn Abbas reads ليال عشر with an annexation meaning nights of ten days.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( والفجر ) والوتر ، ويسر : بالتنوين ، وهو التنوين الذي يقع بدلا من حرف الإطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ in يسر is dropped in connected speech because the kasra suffices, and in pause it is omitted with the kasra; another interpretation means ‘moves along in it.’
rows.anchor: وياء { يسر } تحذف في الدرج ، اكتفاء عنها بالكسرة ، وأما في الوقف فتحذف مع الكسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath objects ask whether these things merit an oath before a rational person, or whether an oath of this magnitude confirms the claim; حجر means intellect because it restrains recklessness.
rows.anchor: { هل فى ذلك } أي فيما أقسمت به من هذه الأشياء { قسم } أي مقسم به { لذى حجر }

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says a person with حجر is one who controls and disciplines himself.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : يقال : إنه لذو حجر ، إذا كان قاهرا لنفسه ضابطا لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted answer to the oath is that God will punish the Meccans for rejecting the Messenger, as indicated by the cited passages.
rows.anchor: والمقسم عليه محذوف وهو ( ليعذبن ) يدل عليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثم marks faith's higher rank and virtue than freeing slaves and charity, not later timing: faith precedes these acts and is necessary for any good deed to stand.
rows.anchor: جاء بثم لتراخي الإيمان وتباعده في الرتبة والفضيلة عن العتق والصدقة ، لا في الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المرحمة means mercy: believers may urge one another to remain firm in faith; to avoid sins, perform duties, and endure trials while showing compassion; or to do what brings God's mercy.
rows.anchor: والمرحمة : الرحمة ، أي : أوصى بعضهم بعضا بالصبر على الإيمان والثبات عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الميمنة and المشأمة mean right and left, or good fortune and ill omen—people fortunate or blameworthy with respect to themselves.
rows.anchor: الميمنة والمشأمة : اليمين والشمال . أو اليمن والشؤم ، أي : الميامين على أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word موصدة is read with a wāw or with hamza; both derive from verbs meaning to shut or close a door.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( موصدة ) بالواو والهمزة ، ومن وصدت الباب وآصدته : إذا أطبقته وأغلقته

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش
rows.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash says their prayer leader uses the hamza reading, and he wishes to cover his ears when he hears it.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي بكر بن عياش : لنا إمام يهمز مؤصدة ؛ فأشتهي أن أسد إذني إذا سمعته

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises safety from God's anger on Judgment Day for whoever recites Surat al-Balad.
rows.anchor: من قرأ لا أقسم بهذا البلد أعطاه الله الأمان من غضبه يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ضحاها is the sun's light once it rises and its power appears; الضحوة is the day's rise, الضحى is later, and الضحاء is the extended day approaching midday.
rows.anchor: ضحاها : ضؤوها إذا أشرقت وقام سلطانها ؛ ولذلك قيل : وقت الضحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon follows the sun by rising as the sun sets and taking its light during the first half of the month; alternatively, it follows when full in brightness.
rows.anchor: { إذا تلاها } طالعا عند غروبها آخذا من نورها ؛ وذلك في النصف الأول من الشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day ‘reveals’ the sun when it swells and spreads and the sun becomes fully clear; the pronoun may instead refer to darkness, the world, or the earth, understood from context.
rows.anchor: { إذا جلاها } عند انتفاخ النهار وانبساطه ، لأن الشمس تنجلي في ذلك الوقت تمام الانجلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night veils the sun, making the horizons dark; the implied object may be inferred just as ‘it became cold’ can imply morning and ‘it rained’ can imply the sky.
rows.anchor: إذا يغشاها ، فتغيب وتظلم الآفاق ، فإن قلت : الأمر في نصب ( إذا ) معضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated wāws can govern both accusative and genitive: the oath-wāw omits its verb altogether and substitutes for it, while coordinated wāws inherit that double function, resolving the apparent two-governor problem.
rows.anchor: واو القسم مطرح معها إبراز الفعل إطراحا كليا ، فكان لها شأن خلاف شأن الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In وما بناها, وما طحاها, and وما سواها, ما is best taken as a relative pronoun, not a verbal noun, which would spoil the sequence; it means the mighty Creator who built and fashioned them.
rows.anchor: جعلت ( ما ) مصدرية في قوله : { وما بناها } { وما طحاها } { وما سواها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite نفس may denote Adam specifically, or all souls, left indefinite to convey abundance as in another verse.
rows.anchor: أن يريد نفسا خاصة من بين النفوس وهي نفس آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inspiring vice and piety means making their difference clear and enabling choice; the following verses show the human being performs purification or defilement, which respectively elevate through piety or diminish through sin.
rows.anchor: ومعنى إلهام الفجور والتقوى : إفهامهما وإعقالهما ، وأن أحدهما حسن والآخر قبيح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Asked about the words, Ibn Abbas points to ‘successful is the one who purifies himself’ and ‘he has failed who bears wrongdoing.’
rows.anchor: أتقرأ : { قد أفلح من تزكى } ، ( الأعلى : 14 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that God is the agent of purifying and defiling is, in the author's view, a distortion by Qadariyya who falsely attribute reprehensible destiny to God.
rows.anchor: وأما قول من زعم أن الضمير في زكى ودسى لله تعالى ، وأن تأنيث الراجع إلى من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath answer is that God will devastate Mecca for rejecting the Messenger, as He devastated Thamud for rejecting Salih; قد أفلح is a digression continuing the preceding point, not the oath answer.
rows.anchor: على أهل مكة لتكذيبهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What the night covers may be the sun, by reference to 91:4; the day, by reference to 13:3; or everything hidden by its darkness, by reference to 113:3.
rows.anchor: المغشي : إما الشمس من قوله : { واليل إذا يغشاها } ( الشمس : 4 ) وإما النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تجلى means appearing as night's darkness passes, or becoming visible as the sun rises.
rows.anchor: { تجلى } ظهر بزوال ظلمة الليل . أو تبين وتكشف بطلوع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Creator may mean the mighty Creator able to make male and female from one fluid, or Adam and Eve; the Prophet's reading says والذكر والأنثى and Ibn Masud reads والذي خلق الذكر والأنثى.
rows.anchor: { وما خلق } والقادر العظيم القدرة الذي قدر على خلق الذكر والأنثى من ماء واحد

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i reads the words الذكر والأنثى in the genitive as an apposition to ما خلق, meaning God's creation; God's name can be omitted because He alone creates.
rows.anchor: وعن الكسائي : ( وما خلق الذكر والأنثى بالجر على أنه بدل من محل { ما خلق }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says every living creature is either male or female; an apparently indeterminate intersex person is known to God as one or the other, so seeing one would break an oath not to see a male or female.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن الله لم يخلق خلقا من ذوي الأرواح ليس بذكر ولا أنثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شتى is the plural of شتيت, meaning different and scattered; the following passage explains how people's endeavors differ.
rows.anchor: { شتى } جمع شتيت ، أي : إن مساعيكم أشتات مختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving means paying wealth's obligations, fearing God means not disobeying Him, and الحسنى may mean faith, Islam, or Paradise.
rows.anchor: يعني حقوق ماله { واتقى } الله فلم يعصه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: We will ease him toward ease means preparing him for it, as a horse is saddled and bridled, and guiding him until obedience becomes easy; compare the promise to open one's heart to Islam.
rows.anchor: فسنهيؤه لها من يسر الفرس للركوب إذا أسرجها وألجمها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says each person is facilitated toward the purpose for which he was created.
rows.anchor: كل ميسر لما خلق له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: استغنى can mean turning away from God's reward as if one did not need Him, and so failing to fear Him; or worldly pleasures can make one feel independent of Paradise's reward, opposite to God-consciousness.
rows.anchor: { واستغنى } وزهد فيما عند الله كأنه مستغن عنه فلم يتقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the person easy for hardship means abandoning and withholding divine assistance until obedience is hardest; alternatively, good and evil paths are named for their outcomes, or they are Paradise and Hell's roads in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: { فسنيسره للعسرى } فسنخذله ونمنعه الألطاف ، حتى تكون الطاعة أعسر شيء عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says these verses concern Abu Bakr and Abu Sufyan ibn Harb.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نزلتا في أبي بكر رضي الله عنه ، وفي أبي سفيان بن حرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما يغني عنه is either a rhetorical question rejecting any benefit from his wealth or a plain negation; تردى can mean death, falling into a grave, or plunging into Hell's depth.
rows.anchor: { وما يغنى عنه } استفهام في معنى الإنكار . أو نفي { تردى } تفعل من الردى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God undertakes guidance by setting out proofs and explaining religious laws.
rows.anchor: الإرشاد إلى الحق واجب علينا بنصب الدلائل وبيان الشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The last and first lives belong to God as reward for the one who follows guidance, as in Abraham's descendants receiving prophecy and scripture.
rows.anchor: أي : ثواب الدارين للمهتدي ، كقوله : { ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise reassures Muhammad, whom the Meccan polytheists mocked for poverty, that God's great gifts mean he should not despair of further favor; ease would come soon after the hardship believers faced.
rows.anchor: كان المشركون يعيرون رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والمؤمنين بالفقر والضيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though مع means accompaniment, the ease follows hardship after a short interval; it is presented as already alongside hardship to console and strengthen hearts.
rows.anchor: أراد أن الله يصيبهم بيسر بعد العسر الذي كانوا فيه بزمان قريب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud say one hardship cannot overcome two eases; the statement is also transmitted as a Prophetic report.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس وابن مسعود رضي الله عنهما : لن يغلب عسر يسرين

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet once came out laughing and said that one hardship would not overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: أنه خرج صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات يوم وهو يضحك ويقول : ( لن يغلب عسر يسرين )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second clause may repeat the first for emphasis, or make a second promise; the definite hardship is the same one, while the indefinite ease can be a different portion, yielding two eases.
rows.anchor: وأن تكون الأولى عدة بأن العسر مردوف بيسر لا محالة ، والثانية عدة مستأنفة بأن العسر متبوع بيسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two eases may be victories in Muhammad's time and the caliphs' time, or ease in this world and the next, as with the two good outcomes of victory and reward.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يراد بهما ما تيسر لهم من الفتوح في أيام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وما تيسر لهم في أيام الخلفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite form magnifies the ease; Ibn Masud's codex has the phrase once, but the Prophetic saying can still take two eases as the ease of both abodes.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت : فما معنى هذا التنكير ؟ قلت : التفخيم ، كأنه قيل : إن مع العسر يسرا عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Figs and olives are wondrous among fruit-bearing trees; reports mention their virtues and use as food and tooth-stick.
rows.anchor: أقسم بهما لأنهما عجيبان من بين أصناف الأشجار المثمرة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet ate a plate of figs, called them a fruit of Paradise if any could be so called, and described them as seedless and beneficial for hemorrhoids and gout.
rows.anchor: وروي : ( 1318 ) أنه أهدي لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم طبق من تين فأكل منه

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: Muadh passed an olive tree, took a branch for brushing his teeth, and said he heard the Prophet praise olive wood as a blessed tooth-stick that freshens the mouth and helps the teeth.
rows.anchor: ومر معاذ بن جبل بشجرة الزيتون فأخذ منها قضيبا واستاك به

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is also reported to say that olive wood was his tooth-stick and that of earlier prophets.
rows.anchor: وسمعته ييقول : ( هي سواكي وسواك الأنبياء قبلي )

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the words as referring to your Prophet and your olives.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : هو نبيكم هذا وزيتونكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the words name two mountains in the Holy Land, called in Syriac Tur Tina and Tur Zayta because figs and olives grow there.
rows.anchor: وقيل : جبلان من الأرض المقدسة يقال لهما بالسريانية : طورتينا وطورزيتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view places the fig mountains between Hulwan and Hamadan, and the olive mountains in Syria, identifying their growing regions.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ( التين ) جبال ما بين حلوان وهمدان . و ( الزيتون ) جبال الشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الطور is a mountain and سينين is the place-name; its inflection can vary like سينون/يبرون, with either case endings or retention of yāʾ and inflection on the nūn.
rows.anchor: وأضيف الطور : وهو الجبل ، إلى سينين : وهي البقعة . ونحو سينون : يبرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure city is Mecca; أمين can mean trustworthy or secure, since it protects entrants, or be passive meaning safe from harm, as in the phrase ‘a secure sanctuary.’
rows.anchor: وللبلد : مكة حماها الله . والأمين : من أمن الرجل أمانة فهو أمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath honors blessed places through the good associated with prophets and righteous people: Abraham migrated to the fig-and-olive region, Jesus was born and raised there, Moses was called at the Mount, and Muhammad was born and sent in Mecca.
rows.anchor: ومعنى القسم بهذه الأشياء : الإبانة عن شرف البقاع المباركة وما ظهر فيها من الخير والبركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أحسن تقويم means the most balanced, beautiful bodily form, with well-proportioned and arranged limbs.
rows.anchor: { فى أحسن تقويم } في أحسن تعديل لشكله وصورته وتسوية لأعضائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أسفل سافلين may mean the ugliest form and composition, the people of Hell, or the lowest of its ranks; alternatively it describes reversal in old age, with a bent back, white hair, wrinkled skin, dulled senses, weak strength, and failing judgment. Abdullah reads أسفل السافلين.
rows.anchor: أن رددناه أسفل من سفل خلقا وتركيبا ، يعني : أقبح من قبح صورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is connected if the return means Hell's lowest ranks, but disconnected if it means old age; righteous elderly still receive unending reward for obedience and patience through frailty.
rows.anchor: هو على الأول متصل ظاهر الاتصال ، وعلى الثاني : منقطع . يعني : ولكن الذين كانوا صالحين من الهرمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question addresses humanity by a shift in person: after clear proof that God created, perfected, developed, and then aged people, what drives denial of resurrection and recompense? An alternative addresses the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قلت : هو خطاب للإنسان على طريقة الالتفات ، أي : فما يجعلك كاذبا بسبب الدين وإنكاره بعد هذا الدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Is God not the wisest of judges?’ threatens disbelievers that God will judge them as they deserve.
rows.anchor: { أليس الله بأحكم الحاكمين } وعيد للكفار ، وأنه يحكم عليهم بما هم أهله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet would answer ‘Indeed, and I am among those who testify to that’ when reciting Surat al-Tin.
rows.anchor: أنه كان إذا قرأها قال : ( بلى وأنا على ذلك من الشاهدين )

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises health and certainty in this life to whoever recites Surat al-Tin, and after death a reward equal to the number of its reciters.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1321 ) ( من قرأ سورة التين أعطاه الله خصلتين : العافية واليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ألهاه and أقهاه mean that something occupied or distracted a person; التكاثر is rivalry and boasting in numbers, each group claiming superiority.
rows.anchor: ألهاه عن كذا وأقهاه : إذا شغله . و { التكاثر } التباري في الكثرة والتباهي بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Banu Abd Manaf and Banu Sahm competed in headcounts; after the former initially outnumbered them, Banu Sahm counted the living and dead and prevailed.
rows.anchor: روي أن بني عبد مناف وبني سهم تفاخروا أيهم أكثر عددا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rivalry continued from counting the living to counting the dead in graves, a mocking description of their competition beyond death; some say they literally visited graves to count and name their dead.
rows.anchor: عبر عن بلوغهم ذكر الموتى بزيارة المقابر تهكما بهم . وقيل : كانوا يزورون المقابر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rivalry may instead be in wealth and children, distracting people until they die and are buried, after spending life pursuing the world instead of religion and the afterlife; visiting graves is a euphemism for death.
rows.anchor: منفقين أعماركم في طلب الدنيا والاستباق إليها والتهالك عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two poetic examples use visiting graves as a figure for dying, including one in which Abu Malik visits graves and becomes the vilest of their visitors.
rows.anchor: زار القبور أبو مالك … فأصبح ألأم زوارها
